research_mode: official Building Safety Regulator and GOV.UK primary guidance only; high-rise accountable-person, risk-assessment, safety-management and resident-engagement methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Safety management system definition
verified_claims: A safety management system is a formal framework for managing safety risks.
limitations: The existence of a framework does not prove that controls are effective.

sources.name: Plan-Do-Check-Act model
verified_claims: One safety-management model uses Plan, Do, Check and Act to set policy, implement controls, measure performance and learn.
limitations: The model is optional and must be adapted to the building.

sources.name: External accreditation not mandatory
verified_claims: A safety management system does not have to be accredited to an external standard; it must work effectively for the organisation and building.
limitations: Absence of accreditation is not evidence of poor performance, and accreditation is not proof of legal compliance.

sources.name: Proportionate safety management
verified_claims: The system should be based on the building risk assessment and proportionate to building complexity, controls, portfolio, organisation, contractors and resident profile.
limitations: A portfolio-wide template must not replace building-specific analysis.

sources.name: Concise and understandable documents
verified_claims: Safety-management documents should be concise and easily understood.
limitations: Brevity must not omit material risk, control or accountability information.

sources.name: Continuous improvement
verified_claims: An effective system regularly reviews and updates controls, policies and procedures and identifies areas for improvement.
limitations: An improvement plan is not evidence that improvements have been delivered.

sources.name: Improvement-plan fields
verified_claims: Improvement plans should state objectives, reasons, timescales, resources and named leaders, with senior managers measuring progress.
limitations: Named ownership does not prove completion or effectiveness.

sources.name: Leadership and resources
verified_claims: Senior leadership should support the system, influence safety culture and provide resources.
limitations: Leadership statements alone are not evidence that resources are sufficient.

sources.name: Roles, competence and authority
verified_claims: Specific safety roles should be defined and supported by competence, training, authority and budgets.
limitations: A job title does not establish competence or authority.

sources.name: Contractor competence controls
verified_claims: Organisations should have systems to verify contractor competence, including appropriate evidence and checks.
limitations: Certification alone does not prove suitability for every task or building.

sources.name: Maintenance scheduling and records
verified_claims: Systems should schedule, undertake and record maintenance and inspection work and retain evidence of completion and remediation.
limitations: A scheduled task is not evidence it was completed correctly or on time.

sources.name: Maintenance-report action tracking
verified_claims: Reports and certificates should be reviewed and identified actions tracked to completion.
limitations: Receipt of a certificate does not prove that all actions were closed.

sources.name: Change-management categories
verified_claims: Change management should cover changes to the building, residents, management systems and changes made by others that affect safety.
limitations: A change category does not establish its actual impact without assessment.

sources.name: Active and reactive monitoring
verified_claims: Effective monitoring uses leading indicators such as timely maintenance and fire-door inspections and lagging indicators such as incidents and breakdowns.
limitations: Indicators must not be averaged in a way that hides individual-building performance.

sources.name: Safety-system review triggers
verified_claims: The system should be reviewed after incidents, performance dips, feedback, complaints, changes to buildings or dutyholders, legal updates and scheduled reviews.
limitations: A review trigger does not itself demonstrate a breach or failure.
